title: Which decimal is greater in each of these three pairs?
description: Three pairs of decimals are compared from the left, one place at a time, including a pair where the greater number ends in zeroes. Keeko doubts the second pair and thinks 3.81 is greater than 13.800.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare the whole parts first, then go place by place from the left. Watch for students who compare only the digits after the point.

video_script.why: The child has compared two decimals place by place and now meets pairs with different lengths and zeroes.
video_script.substitution: Compare the highest place first, and move right until the digits differ.
video_script.anchor: the three pairs of decimals of the book: 1.23 and 1.32, 3.81 and 13.800, 1.009 and 1.090
video_script.wrong_answer: three point eight one is greater
video_script.wrong_move: Compares only the digits after the point, so thinks 3.81 beats 13.800.
video_script.payoff_line: Whole parts first, and then place by place

final_answer.spoken: in the first pair one point three two, in the second pair thirteen point eight zero zero, in the third pair one point zero nine zero

maths_rules: 1.23 and 1.32: units equal, tenths 2 < 3, so 1.32 is greater
1.009 and 1.090: units equal, tenths 0 and 0, hundredths 0 < 9, so 1.090 is greater
video_script.design: Each pair stands in digit columns. The deciding column is boxed in an accent colour and the greater number gets a tick.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three pairs of decimals: 1.23 or 1.32, 3.81 or 13.800, 1.009 or 1.090
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about three pairs of decimals.
<bookmark mark='p1'/>The first pair is one point two three and one point three two.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>The second pair is three point eight one and thirteen point eight zero zero.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>The third pair is one point zero zero nine and one point zero nine zero. Which is greater in each pair?

beats.on_screen: the three pairs stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the three pairs

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: digit columns: tens | units | . | tenths | hundredths | thousandths; compare from the left

marks.cols: the digit columns are drawn with the point in place
marks.left: an arrow runs from the highest place to the right

narration: <bookmark mark='cols'/>We write each pair in columns, lined up on the point.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Then we compare from the highest place, and move right until the digits differ.

marks.given: the three pairs are written in columns

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three pairs of decimals, written in columns.

beats.on_screen: To find: the greater decimal in each pair
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the greater decimal in each pair.

beats.on_screen: 1.23 and 1.32: units 1 and 1, equal; tenths 2 and 3, 3 > 2, so 1.32 is greater

marks.t: the tenths column differs and the larger digit is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='u'/>Step one, take the first pair. The units are one and one, so they are equal.
<bookmark mark='t'/>The tenths are two and three. Three is greater, so one point three two is greater.

beats.on_screen: 3.81 and 13.800: tens 0 and 1, 1 > 0, so 13.800 is greater

marks.tens: the tens column differs and the one is circled
marks.zeros: the zeroes at the end of thirteen point eight zero zero fade to grey

narration: <bookmark mark='tens'/>Step two, take the second pair. Start at the tens place. Three point eight one has no tens, but thirteen point eight zero zero has one ten.
<bookmark mark='zeros'/>The zeroes at the end do not matter. Thirteen point eight zero zero is greater.

beats.on_screen: 1.009 and 1.090: units 1 and 1; tenths 0 and 0; hundredths 0 and 9, 9 > 0, so 1.090 is greater

marks.same: the units and tenths columns match
marks.h: the hundredths column differs and the nine is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step three, take the third pair. The units are equal, and the tenths are both zero.
<bookmark mark='h'/>The hundredths are zero and nine. Nine is greater, so one point zero nine zero is greater.

marks.vals: the three greater numbers are ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Whole parts first, and then place by place.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>The greater numbers are one point three two and thirteen point eight zero zero. The third is one point zero nine zero.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the three pairs
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: 3.81 > 13.800 since 81 > 8; 13.800 has a tens digit; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the tens digit of thirteen point eight zero zero glows
marks.rule: the tens place is placed above all places to its right

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three point eight one is greater, since eighty one is more than eight.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But thirteen point eight zero zero has one ten, and three point eight one has none.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The tens place is worth more than every place to its right.
